root_idea.summary: The root centers on standing upright or remaining firmly fixed, often with an implication of persistence or adherence.
root_idea.development: From upright, fixed posture, the lexical development extends to sticking or clinging fast, becoming elevated or projecting, poised tiptoe posture, and related derived actions such as mutual lifting.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Quranic noun citation form جَذْوَة.

senses.definition: A piece of firewood remaining after burning, especially a live ember or firebrand.
senses.usage_conditions: In أَوْ جَذْوَةٍ مِنَ النَّارِ, it denotes a portion taken from a fire; the classical descriptions include a glowing or flaming coal and firewood that remains after the flames have subsided.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stand or remain firmly; to be or become erect and straight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May be used of a thing or living being, including remaining firm upon something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stick or cling fast to something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of something adhering tightly to another object, as a tick clinging to a camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stand poised on the extremities of the toes; in variant usage, to sit on the knees or heels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a bird standing on tiptoe while warbling and circling, and to a horse or person standing on the toes; authorities distinguish this posture from sitting on the knees.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel’s hump, to become filled with fat and elevated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use describing the raised, fat-bearing hump.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be raised, extended, or projecting outward.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the nostrils and, in a bodily description, of an elbow standing out from the side.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a young camel, to bear fat in its hump.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV usage describing the development of a fat, elevated hump.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lift a stone in order to test or display strength.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The action may be performed competitively, with people taking turns or striving to lift the stone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To vie with one another in lifting a stone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VI construction for competing or assisting one another in the stone-lifting trial.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To raise one’s eye or sight and cast it before oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used transitively with the eye or gaze directed ahead.
An active participle of جَذَا; applied, for example, to supports or stones that remain in place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Poised on the knees, heels, or tips of the toes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The participial posture term has variant descriptions among authorities, ranging from kneeling or sitting on the heels to standing on tiptoe.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of she-camels, carrying themselves erect in their gait, with the feet lifted clear from the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied specifically to she-camels; one reported interpretation emphasizes swiftness, while another emphasizes their erect carriage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Firm and erect upon the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participle of Form IV, used in a simile of a tree that stands firmly and uprightly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Keeping constantly attached to a dwelling or to a camel’s saddle and not leaving it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes persistent adherence to a place or riding gear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who lowers or abases himself, as though clinging to the ground from abjectness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative characterization derived from the notion of sticking closely to the ground.

cautions: The noun is recorded with variant classical vocalizations جِذْوَة, جُذْوَة, and جَذْوَة; the public headword follows the Quranic form supplied by QAC and the Quran-focused evidence.
The interpretation of جَوَاذٍ varies in the classical evidence between erect carriage with lifted feet and swiftness.
